title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum
authors: Ferenc Bencs, Brice Huang, Daniel Z. Lee, Kuikui Liu, Guus Regts
abstract: We give the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the uniformly random $d$-regular graph to arbitrarily high accuracy for all inverse temperatures up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold. This is the entire regime in which the model is "replica symmetric," and is conjectured to be optimal for polynomial-time counting and sampling. To achieve our algorithmic result, we establish the absence of Fisher zeros for the partition function in a constant-width strip around the interval from $0$ up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, with high probability over the randomness of the input graph. summary: This paper presents a breakthrough polynomial-time algorithm to accurately estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on random graphs up to a critical temperature threshold. The core mathematical achievement is proving the absence of zeros for the partition function in a specific complex region. This work advances the understanding of computational tractability in disordered quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop efficient algorithms for the approximate counting of the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on random regular graphs.
main_result: The authors provide the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, contingent on proving the absence of Fisher zeros in a specific complex strip.
method: The primary method involves adapting Barvinok’s interpolation technique, supported by rigorous proofs establishing moment bounds and zero-freeness for the partition function.
model_or_system: The system is the Ising model defined by the Hamiltonian $H_G(\sigma) = \sum_{u v \in E}  rac{1 - \sigma_u \sigma_v}{2}$ on a uniformly random $d$-regular graph $G$. The focus is on the antiferromagnetic case ($ eta \ge 0$).
key_observables: The partition function $Z_G( eta)$, the quenched free energy, and the location of Fisher zeros.
important_parameters: The inverse temperature $ eta$, the graph degree $d$, and the Kesten-Stigum threshold $ eta_{KS}(d)$.
main_assumptions: The results are established for the average-case setting (random graphs) and rely on the conjecture that the regime $ eta \le  eta_{KS}(d)$ is optimally solvable in polynomial time.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the main algorithmic result (Theorem 1.1) based on zero-free regions (Theorem 1.2), utilizing advanced techniques like moment bounds and lattice summation formulas (e.g., Poisson Summation Formula) to prove the necessary analytic properties.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the techniques developed—especially the use of complex analysis, zero-free regions, and polynomial-time counting algorithms for partition functions—are highly relevant to understanding the complexity and computational limits of quantum many-body systems.
